drivingQuestion: Whence is it derived that one who touches a sealed thigh bone of a carcass remains pure?
outcomeNote: The baraita supplies the verse from which the mishna's exemption of a sealed thigh bone follows; the derivation is carried on in the next unit.

segments.he: קוּלִית נְבֵלָה וְקוּלִית הַשֶּׁרֶץ וְכוּ׳. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״בְּנִבְלָתָהּ״ – וְלֹא בְּקוּלִית סְתוּמָה.
segments.en: §The mishna teaches: With regard to «the thigh bone of an unslaughtered carcass and the thigh bone of a creeping animal,» one who touches them when they are sealed remains ritually pure, because the bone itself does not impart impurity. With regard to this topic, «the Sages taught» in a baraita: The verse states: “One who touches the carcass thereof shall be impure until the evening” (Leviticus 11:39). The word «“carcass”» indicates that one who touches the carcass is impure, «but» one who touches «a sealed thigh bone is not.»
